newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's Yilmaz takes over from Islamist Erbakan.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's Yilmaz takes over from Islamist Erbakan.

text.p: Turkish secularist Mesut Yilmaz took over the post of prime minister from outgoing Islamist Necmettin Erbakan at a ceremony on Monday.
A smiling Erbakan shook hands with Yilmaz at the short ceremony in the prime minister's office, bringing the curtain down on Turkey's first Islamist-led government.
Yilmaz thanked his opponent. "I would like to thank the prime minister and his colleagues for a year of service," he said.
President Suleyman Demirel appointed Yilmaz earlier in the day to replace Erbakan, who resigned two weeks ago amid disputes with the secularist army over Islamist activism.
The ceremony took place a year and a day after Erbakan himself took over the prime minister's seat as the first Islamist to govern NATO member Turkey.
Yilmaz, 50, heads a left-right coalition that faces a confidence vote in parliament in around 10 days' time.
His bid to build a government excluding Erbakan's Islam-based Welfare Party has been boosted by a wave of defections from a conservative faction allied with the Islamists.
Yilmaz now has around 12 more MPs on paper than his opponents in the 550-member national assembly.
